beats.narration_text: Prot2Vec is a benchmark harness for protein sequence embeddings. This week it went from two representations to nine, from two projections to thirteen, and from ten metrics to thirty-one. This is Sai. The interesting part is not the breadth. It is that the release added three new ways to catch a result that is secretly measuring something else — and then caught its own.

show.event: the ask types in; the three headline counts land as result lines
the test count fills in beneath them
the last line lands alone and holds

props.command: Prot2Vec shipped v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 in one week: nine representations, thirteen projections, thirty-one metrics, 411 tests. Don't tell me it got bigger. Tell me what the new metrics are defending against — and whether the instrument doing the measuring was itself being measured.
props.runningText: reading back what the release actually measured…
output: and one measurement that was lying

beats.narration_text: So, what is it. You hand it sequences with group labels. It runs every embedding method against every dimensionality reducer and scores all of them with the same metrics, so the comparison is actually like for like. Nine ways to turn a sequence into a vector, from counting amino acids to calling a protein language model. Six of the nine need no PyTorch at all.

show.event: the six dependency-free descriptors fill the first two rows
the three learned representations complete the grid
the caption settles — compute once, project thirteen ways

props.sparkLine: NINE WAYS TO TURN A SEQUENCE INTO A VECTOR
props.caption: Each embedding is computed once and reused across all thirteen projections

beats.narration_text: Here is the metric that sets the tone for the whole release. Neighbourhood preservation asks what fraction of each point's true nearest neighbours survive the projection. But that number has a floor. Even a projection carrying no information keeps some neighbours by luck — k over n minus one of them. So the release ships the chance-corrected version, and subtracts the floor.

show.event: the raw overlap NP(k) typesets first — a fraction bar and a sum over all n points
LCMC appears beneath it: the same quantity with the chance term subtracted
the floor is evaluated for the README's own run — 10 of 89, about 0.1124

props.title: What would a projection carrying nothing have scored?
props.note: Chance-corrected neighbourhood overlap. Zero means no better than luck.
props.conditions: n points, k neighbours, k < n. Verified on 40 seeded random pairs with the shipped function: NP = 0.109 ± 0.011 against a predicted 0.1124, LCMC = −0.003.

beats.narration_text: And this is the failure the harness exists to catch. Two protein families separate cleanly on screen. That can mean the representation found real homology. Or it can mean the representation encoded sequence length, and length happens to differ between those families. In a scatter plot those two look identical. The confound group added this week refuses to let them.

show.event: one split starts from the same observed separation
the upper track survives every control and stays real structure
the lower track resolves to length in disguise

data.slideMeta: IT CLUSTERED NICELY · TWO CAUSES THAT LOOK THE SAME

tracks.label: a confound
notes: length alone scores just as well

beats.narration_text: Then the same release caught its own instrument. Coverage had been told to ignore any line that is just an ellipsis — the abstract-method placeholder. The pattern was never anchored. So it also matched a type annotation, tuple of string, ellipsis, and coverage discards the entire statement a matching line belongs to. Sixty-one statements quietly left the report. Forty-seven of them sat in the module that scores everything else.

show.event: suite.py lands first with 47 hidden statements
cli.py and pipeline.py follow, two orders of magnitude smaller
the tree total closes the table at 61 — a headline number that moved barely three points

props.title: Statements the unanchored exclude pattern hid
props.note: Recorded output — coverage 7.8.2 parsing prot2vec v0.3.0 under the v0.2.0 exclude entry. suite.py measured 13 of its 60 statements; evaluate() was one of the hidden ones. evidence/coverage_exclusion.py

beats.narration_text: Breadth also changes what a single bug costs. NMF refuses signed input. A manifold method can fail on a disconnected neighbour graph. At four pairs those are exceptions; across a full matrix they are ordinary. Previously any one of them discarded every pair that had already succeeded. That was the fork this week actually turned on.

show.event: the question splits into the two handling strategies
the abort branch shows what it costs — the successful pairs go too
the resolver reframes the failures as expected traffic

data.slideMeta: A FULL MATRIX · ONE PAIR RAISES
data.question: Abort the run, or isolate the pair?

branches.label: Let the exception rise
branches.detail: one bad pair ends the whole matrix

branches.label: Isolate per pair
branches.detail: record it, name it, keep the rest

resolver.label: The failures are not exceptional
resolver.detail: a rejected sign, a disconnected graph, a missing optional backend — at this width they are expected traffic, so a run now raises only when every single pair has failed

data.ghostText: a skipped pair is a result you can cite, not a crash you rerun around

beats.narration_text: So: two releases, one week. The breadth is the headline. The defences are the release. And the coverage bug is the part worth keeping, because it is the same mistake the whole tool exists to find — a number that looked fine while quietly measuring less than it claimed.

show.event: the artifact card opens and the two releases are stated as one page
the defences line and the coverage line fill in beneath
the test count closes it

artifactLines: Two releases landed in one week. v0.2.0 made it an installable package with FASTA input, a run manifest and a chance baseline printed beside every score. v0.3.0 took it to nine representations, thirteen projections and thirty-one metrics, across protein, DNA and RNA.

Most of the new metrics are defences. random_projection is a control that fits nothing. LCMC subtracts the neighbourhood overlap luck alone would have produced. The confound group reports the accuracy reachable from sequence length alone, and the CLI warns when a result is explained by it.

The coverage exclude pattern was unanchored, so it matched tuple[str, ...] and discarded the statement that line belonged to. 61 statements were never measured — 47 of them in suite.py, the module that scores everything else. Anchoring the pattern restored them.
411 tests, up from 208. One invalid pair no longer aborts the matrix: it is isolated, named in the output, and recorded under skipped_pairs in the run manifest.

beats.narration_text: Your turn, and you can run this against anything you are about to publish. Here is a benchmark result. Before you tell me whether the score is good, tell me what a random control would have scored on the same data, what the result becomes if the representation encodes only length, and whether the tooling I used to check my own work is itself being checked. Then tell me which one I forgot.

show.event: the handoff prompt types in under 'Your turn.'
the three checks stack as the prompt fills
the final clause lands and the cursor holds

props.command: Here is a benchmark result I am about to publish. Before you tell me whether the score is good, tell me three things: what a random control would have scored on the same data, what the result becomes if the representation encodes only sequence length, and whether the tooling I used to check my own work is itself being checked. Then tell me which of those three I forgot.
